next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Michigan Department of State — How to Vote in Michigan

glance_notes.source_name: Michigan Department of State — How to Vote in Michigan
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadlines: The deadline to register online or by mail for Michigan's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 19. From October 20 through Election Day, eligible residents may still register in person at their city or township clerk's office or satellite office with proof of residency.

glance_notes.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Early In-Person Voting
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 24–November 1: Michigan's constitutionally required early voting period for the November 3, 2026 General Election runs from October 24 through November 1. Communities may provide additional early-voting days, and beginning in 2026 they may also offer early voting on the Monday before Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Every registered Michigan voter has the right to vote by absentee ballot without providing a reason. Michigan also allows voters to join a permanent absentee ballot list and automatically receive an absentee ballot for future elections.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Michigan residents may register online, by mail or in person when there are at least 15 days before an election. Within 14 days of Election Day, including Election Day itself, registration must be completed in person at the voter's city or township clerk's office or an authorized satellite office, with proof of residency. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, a Michigan resident, a resident of the applicable city or township for at least 30 days by Election Day, and at least 17 years and 6 months old. A person must be 18 years old by Election Day to vote.
register.glance_value: Online, mail or in person; same-day registration available
register.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Michigan's official registration guidance establishes online, mail and in-person registration and the special in-person procedure beginning 14 days before an election. The Department of State identifies Michigan residence, city/township residence for at least 30 days by Election Day, citizenship and age requirements. Within 14 days, proof of residency is required.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Michigan Voter Information Center at Michigan.gov/Vote to check your voter registration, find your polling place and early voting site, view a sample ballot when available, locate your local clerk and track an absentee ballot.
check_registration.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Michigan Voter Information Center
check_registration.internal_note: Michigan.gov/Vote is the Department of State's official voter information service. State guidance directs voters there for registration status, clerk information, polling places, early voting sites, sample ballots and absentee ballot tracking.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For Michigan's November 3, 2026 General Election, October 19 is the last day to register online or by mail. Beginning October 20, new registrations must be completed in person at the voter's city or township clerk's office or satellite office with proof of residency. Eligible residents may register in person through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is in line at the clerk's office by 8:00 p.m. may complete registration and vote.
deadlines.glance_value: Online/mail by October 19; in person through Election Day
deadlines.source_name: Michigan Department of State — How to Vote in Michigan
deadlines.internal_note: The Department of State's current November 2026 election information directly establishes October 19 as the online/mail deadline and October 20-November 3 as the period when new registrations must be completed in person. The registration page confirms the 8:00 p.m. Election Day deadline and proof-of-residency requirement.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Michigan.gov/Vote to find the Election Day polling place assigned to your registered address. Michigan voters casting a ballot on Election Day generally vote at their assigned precinct polling place. Early voting uses designated early voting sites that may be different from Election Day polling places, so voters should verify the correct location for the method and date they plan to vote.
polling_place.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Michigan Voter Information Center
polling_place.internal_note: Michigan's voter information center provides voter-specific polling-place information. Early voting locations are separately published and may serve multiple jurisdictions, so Election Day and early-voting locations should not be treated as interchangeable.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Michigan's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. local time. Anyone in line by 8:00 p.m. has the right to vote. Voters are asked to show an acceptable photo ID when voting in person, but a registered voter who does not have acceptable photo identification may still vote after signing an affidavit. Eligible residents may also register to vote in person at their city or township clerk's office through 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
election_day.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Voting on Election Day
election_day.internal_note: Michigan polling hours are 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. local time. Michigan spans Eastern and Central time zones, so local time matters. Michigan's voter-ID procedure permits a voter without photo identification to sign an affidavit and vote a regular ballot rather than being categorically denied a ballot.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Michigan polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. local time on Election Day. Voters who are in line at their polling place by 8:00 p.m. are entitled to cast a ballot.
polling_hours.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Voting on Election Day
polling_hours.internal_note: The statewide Election Day hours are 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Michigan has communities in both Eastern and Central time zones, so the legally relevant time is local time.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Michigan provides early in-person voting for statewide and federal elections. The constitutionally required early voting period for the November 3, 2026 General Election runs for nine consecutive days from October 24 through November 1. Communities may choose to provide additional early-voting days, up to 29 days total, and beginning in 2026 may also provide early voting on Monday, November 2. Each early voting site must be open for at least eight hours on each required early-voting day. Exact locations and hours vary by community and are available through Michigan.gov/Vote.
early_voting.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The Department of State directly establishes the mandatory nine-day period beginning the second Saturday before Election Day and ending the Sunday before Election Day. The state's November 2026 election page specifically identifies October 24-November 1. Communities may offer up to 29 days total and, beginning in 2026, may optionally offer Monday-before-Election-Day early voting. Locations, dates and hours are available up to 60 days before Election Day.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Michigan voter may vote by absentee ballot without providing a reason. Voters may request an absentee ballot online, by mail or from their local clerk and may choose to join Michigan's permanent absentee ballot list to automatically receive an absentee ballot for future elections. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, absentee ballots become available September 24. Voters may return a completed ballot by mail, authorized drop box, in person to their local clerk, or at an eligible early voting site during the early-voting period. Ordinary domestic absentee ballots must be received by the voter's local clerk by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day to be counted.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; ballots available September 24
absentee_mail.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Department of State confirms no-excuse absentee voting and the permanent absentee ballot list. The November 2026 election page identifies September 24 as the date absentee ballots become available. Ordinary domestic absentee ballots must reach the local clerk by 8:00 p.m. Election Day. Military and overseas ballots have a separate postmark-and-receipt rule documented in military_overseas.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Michigan voters are asked to show an acceptable photo ID when voting in person. Accepted documents include a Michigan driver's license or state ID, a driver's license or state ID issued by another state, a federal or state government-issued photo ID, a U.S. passport, military photo ID, student photo ID from an accredited high school or postsecondary institution, or a tribal identification card with a photo. The document does not need to show the voter's address. A registered voter who does not have acceptable photo identification may still vote by signing an affidavit stating that the voter is not in possession of photo ID.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID requested; affidavit option available
voter_id.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Voting on Election Day
voter_id.internal_note: Michigan should not be described as having an absolute photo-ID requirement. State law asks voters to present photo identification but expressly permits a registered voter without acceptable photo ID to sign an affidavit and cast a regular ballot. Student and tribal photo IDs are among the accepted categories.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Michigan voters with disabilities have the right to accessible polling places, accessible voting equipment and assistance with voting. Accessible voting devices are available for voters who need help reading or marking a ballot privately and independently. Voters may receive assistance from a person of their choice, subject to federal restrictions involving an employer or union representative. Michigan also provides accessible absentee-ballot options for voters with qualifying disabilities. The Michigan Bureau of Elections has an Ombudsperson for Accessible Elections who can assist voters experiencing accessibility problems.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible locations, equipment, assistance and absentee options
accessible_voting.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: Michigan's Elections Bureau provides dedicated accessibility resources and an Ombudsperson for Accessible Elections at 517-335-2730. The state provides accessible voting equipment and accessible absentee-voting procedures. Local clerks should be contacted about location-specific accommodations.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Michigan provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible military members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot, and the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available as a backup. For the November 3, 2026 election, Michigan's federal military and overseas ballot-transmission deadline is September 19. A completed Federal Post Card Application may be returned to the local clerk by email, fax or mail and must be received by 2:00 p.m. on the Saturday before Election Day. Military and overseas voters may receive ballots electronically. Beginning in 2025, certain eligible active-duty military members and merchant mariners outside the United States may also return voted ballots electronically through Michigan's secure portal after satisfying the state's identity-verification requirements. Other overseas voters must return voted ballots by mail. Qualifying mailed military and overseas ballots are counted if postmarked by Election Day and received within six days after the election.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, electronic delivery and limited electronic return
military_overseas.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Michigan's current military/overseas guidance establishes FPCA and FWAB use, the 2:00 p.m. Saturday application deadline, electronic ballot delivery and the six-day post-election receipt period for ballots postmarked by Election Day. The November 2026 election page establishes September 19 as the MOVE transmission deadline. Electronic return is not available to all overseas voters: it is limited to statutorily eligible military members and merchant mariners using a Department of Defense Common Access Card signature through the Electronic Delivery and Return Portal.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may choose the Michigan residence they use for voting according to the state's residency rules. A Michigan resident attending school in another state may remain registered at a Michigan home address and vote absentee or may choose to register at the out-of-state campus address if eligible there. A student from another state attending college or university in Michigan may register using a Michigan campus address if the student chooses to establish that address as the voting residence. A student may vote in only one state in a single election.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may choose one qualifying home or campus residence
student_voting.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Student Voting
student_voting.internal_note: The dedicated Department of State student-voting page expressly confirms that Michigan residents attending school elsewhere may vote from their Michigan home address or register at an eligible campus address in the other state. Out-of-state students attending a Michigan institution may register at their Michigan campus address. The state expressly warns that students may vote in only one state during a single election.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Michigan voters can view their personalized sample ballot through the Michigan Voter Information Center at Michigan.gov/Vote when ballots are available. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's residential address, precinct and electoral districts, voters should use their own registration information to retrieve the sample ballot that applies to them.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your sample ballot at Michigan.gov/Vote
sample_ballot.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Michigan Voter Information Center
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Department of State's early-voting guidance specifically directs voters to Michigan.gov/Vote to review their sample ballot. Candidate and ballot information continues to develop before the November election, so this section should be reverified closer to Election Day.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Michigan Department of State, Bureau of Elections. Elections information phone: 800-292-5973. Email: Elections@Michigan.gov. Regular Bureau of Elections hours are Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., although hours may change during elections and deadline periods. The Ombudsperson for Accessible Elections can be reached at 517-335-2730. For questions about an individual registration record, polling location, early voting site or absentee ballot, voters should contact their city or township clerk.
contact.source_name: Michigan Department of State — Bureau of Elections
contact.internal_note: The current Bureau of Elections page directly verifies 800-292-5973, [Elections@Michigan.gov](mailto:Elections@Michigan.gov), weekday 8:00 a.m.-4:45 p.m. regular hours and the 517-335-2730 accessible-elections Ombudsperson number. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Michigan Department of State Elections website and Michigan.gov/Vote for official statewide election information. Michigan.gov/Vote provides voter registration information, polling places, early voting sites, sample ballots, local clerk information and absentee-ballot tracking. Michigan's city and township clerks administer voter registration and many local voting functions, including absentee ballots, Election Day polling places and early voting services.
official_resources.glance_value: Department of State, Michigan.gov/Vote & local clerks
official_resources.internal_note: Official November 2026 election information: [https://www.michigan.gov/sos/elections/voting](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/elections/voting).
